correctness.rationale: The finite certificates contain precisely all 169 or 238 maximal faces (complements of disconnected triples) at n=13,14. For each successive facet F, the ridge set R(F) is nonempty and not contained in any earlier facet, which is equivalent to the pure shelling condition by the proved lemma. Direct independent intersection coverage and graph-connectivity checks reproduce the conclusions, the complete numbers of nonempty faces 7904 and 16067, and 1 and 8 spanning facets. For n>=15 Theorem 1.4 of arXiv:2603.23155 (p=3) supplies shellability and the same formula. Limit: only the two finite orders have newly supplied certificates; the larger-order theorem is cited rather than reproved.

originality.rationale: The new assertion is shellability at n=13,14. The 2024 Conjecture 4.2 predicts it and its homology Table 2 reports the ranks, but neither yields facet-order shellability. The 2026 Theorem 1.4 starts at n>=15 when p=3. Relevant indexed-result searches and the accessible historical claim ledgers did not identify a previously established n=13/14 shelling or a stronger general theorem; closest mathematically distinct claims concern p=2, total cuts, or n>=15. Residual unindexed overlap is acknowledged.

value.rationale: A specific published positive shellability conjecture predicted the exact threshold n>=4p+1. The 2026 theorem proved p=3 only for n>=15. Exhaustive pure shellings for precisely n=13 and n=14 finish the natural finite gap, yielding the full positive conjectural range p=3,n>=13. This proves a structural property strictly stronger than known homology and is not an arbitrary numerical perturbation or known-table recomputation. It does not claim the remaining negative branch or p>=4.
